experiment_description: A reduced coherent detector blinding attack was performed on a real locally generated local-oscillator continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) receiver, with the transmitter omitted and the exploitation stage emulated by an incoherent optical noise source. The target receiver used an Aerodiode 1550 nm DFB Model 5 laser as the local oscillator, driven by a Wavelength Electronics MPL250 laser driver and PTC2.5K-CH temperature controller. The LO path and signal path each contained an Agiltron LightBend 1x1 optical switch, allowing acquisition of thermal-noise data with both paths closed, shot-noise data with only the LO path open, and noisy data with both paths open. In the polarization-diverse receiver, the LO was split by a polarizing beam splitter with its fast axis shifted by 45 degrees relative to the LO polarization so that half the LO power went to each 50/50 polarization-maintaining beamsplitter. The incoming signal/noise path was split by a second PBS and mixed with the LO components in the two 50/50 beamsplitters. The two balanced detector outputs were measured using Wieserlabs WL-BPD1GA balanced optical receivers with 1.6 GHz bandwidth and AC cutoff below 300 kHz, digitized by a Texas Instruments ADC12DJ3200EVM at 3.2 GHz, and processed on a PC. The reduced DSP downconverted the region around 400 MHz to baseband by multiplying the time-domain signal by exp(-i 2 pi 400e6 t), filtered both polarization components with a root-raised-cosine filter with roll-off factor 0.95 and symbol rate 153.6 MBaud, combined the two polarizations using a polarization-drift-recovery method assuming equal distribution between receiver arms, and computed the recovered-signal variance. Noise was reported in shot-noise units (SNU), where SNU is defined as Var[shot] - Var[thermal], Var[shot] is the DSP variance when only the LO path is open, and Var[thermal] is the DSP variance when both optical paths are closed. For a noisy acquisition, sigma_tilde_squared = Var[noisy]/SNU, epsilon_th = Var[thermal]/SNU, and the estimated excess noise in SNU was computed as epsilon_tilde = (sigma_tilde_squared - 1 - epsilon_th)/(eta*T), with receiver efficiency eta = 0.90 and assumed channel transmission T = 0.5, corresponding to 15 km of standard single-mode fibre; no finite-size effects were included. The incoherent noise source used a Thorlabs EDFA100S erbium-doped fibre amplifier with no input signal, exploiting amplified spontaneous emission, followed by a Thorlabs V1550A voltage-controlled variable optical attenuator driven by a UNI-T UDP3305S supply under PC serial control. The noise was combined through a WBC-2x2-13/15-10/90 90/10 beamsplitter, with optical power monitored on the 90% output by an OZ-Optics POM-300 and corrected to the 10% injected-output value. During the attack demonstration, the noise source was held at five constant corrected optical noise powers: -27.0 dBm, -28.3 dBm, -29.9 dBm, -30.8 dBm, and -31.8 dBm. The blinding source used a Sumitomo Electric Industries SLV5410 diode emitting at 1344 nm, current-driven by a Rigol DG1032 function generator and temperature-controlled by a Thorlabs TED200C. The diode was directly modulated with a 10 MHz square-wave pattern to bypass the receiver AC coupling. The blinding beam passed through a Thorlabs V1550A VOA controlled by a UNI-T UDP3305S, then through a Thorlabs TD1315R5F1 dual-window 1310/1550 nm 50/50 beamsplitter, with one output monitored by an OZ Optics POM-600 and the other combined with the signal/noise path in a Thorlabs WD1350B wavelength-division multiplexer. A polarization controller adjusted the 1344 nm blinding polarization so that both balanced receiver arms received approximately equal blinding amplitude, as judged by the balanced-detector outputs. For each fixed noise-source power, the 1344 nm blinding power was swept from -15.64536 dBm to -12.53858 dBm. The criterion for hiding the attack was that the receiver-estimated excess noise fall below the maximum tolerable excess noise for positive secret-key rate for a probabilistically shaped 64-QAM CV-QKD protocol using a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, channel transmission T = 0.5, and the asymptotic security proof of Denys, Brown, and Leverrier.

maximum_tolerable_excess_noise_for_posit.description: Security-analysis threshold for the described probabilistically shaped 64-QAM CV-QKD operating point; receiver-estimated excess noise below this value would lead the system to report a positive key rate. Units are shot-noise units relative to the measured vacuum shot-noise variance.

hidden_excess_noise_level_1_snu.description: One experimentally introduced excess-noise level that the blinding attack could hide, expressed in shot-noise units relative to the receiver shot-noise calibration.

blinding_power_to_hide_excess_noise_leve.description: Minimum reported 1344 nm square-wave-modulated blinding optical power sufficient to reduce the receiver-estimated excess noise for hidden_excess_noise_level_1_snu below the positive-key-rate excess-noise threshold.
